newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Kellogg off, Campbell gains.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Kellogg off, Campbell gains.

text.p: Kellogg Co shares continued to fall preceding Thursday's U.S. market open, extending losses that began last night when the company said third-quarter and full year results would be eroded by cereal price reductions.
Ahead of the opening bell, Kellogg was active at 64-1/4, down from 68-1/2 at the New York Stock Exchange close on Wednesday and below the 66-1/8 hit in after-hours trade.
Shares in another food giant, Campbell Soup Co, traded higher on news of $2.5 billion in share repurchases and a corporate restructuring.
Campbell rose 1-3/8 to 68-7/8 before the market open.
Kellogg said the cereal price war sweeping through its industry would trim third quarter earnings by about 20 percent from the $1.05 a share earned in the year-ago period.
It also said it expects earnings to resume growth in the fourth quarter, although full-year earnings will fall short of the $3.48 a share netted in 1995.
Campbell said the share buyback would be conducted through a $1.5 billion Dutch auction followed by $1 billion in open market share repurchases.
It said it would take an after-tax charge of about $160 million for restructuring and related expenses.
The moves, which include the expected sale of various plant operations and non-strategic assets, are expected to save $200 million over the next two years, the company said.
